UKBB:Income score (England).name: Income score (England)
UKBB:Income score (England).text:
This domain measures the proportion of the population in an area experiencing deprivation related to low income. A combined count of income deprived individuals per LSOA is calculated by summing the following five indicators:
  • Adults and children in Income Support families
  • Adults and children in Income-Based Jobseeker's Allowance families
  • Adults and children in Pension Credit (Guarantee) families
  • Adults and children in Child Tax Credit families (who are not in receipt of Income Support, Income-Based Jobseeker's Allowance or Pension Credit) whose equivalised income (excluding housing benefits) is below 60 per cent of the median before housing costs
  • Asylum seekers in England in receipt of subsistence support, accommodation support, or both.

UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Engl.name: Index of Multiple Deprivation (England)
UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Engl.text:
The English Indices of Deprivation 2010 are measures of multiple deprivation at the small area level. The model of multiple deprivation which underpins the Indices of Deprivation 2010 is based on the idea of distinct domains of deprivation which can be recognised and measured separately. These domains are experienced by individuals living in an area. People may be counted in one or more of the domains, depending on the number of types of deprivation that they experience.

Each domain represents a specific form of deprivation experienced by people and each can be measured individually using a number of indicators. Seven distinct domains have been identified in the English Indices of Deprivation; Income Deprivation, Employment Deprivation, Health Deprivation and Disability, Education Skills and Training Deprivation, Barriers to Housing and Services, Living Environment Deprivation, and Crime. Individual domains can be used in isolation as measures of each specific form of deprivation. They can also be combined, using appropriate weights, into a single overall Index of Multiple Deprivation which can be used to rank every small area in England according to the deprivation experienced by the people living there. Along with two supplementary indices, Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index and Income Deprivation Affecting Older People Index, they form the English Indices of Deprivation. These statistics allow the most, and least, deprived areas of the country to be identified as well as providing information about the issues faced by people living in different parts of the country.

UKBB:Income score (Wales).name: Income score (Wales)
UKBB:Income score (Wales).text:
The purpose of this domain is to capture the extent of deprivation relating to income at a small area level across Wales. It focuses on the proportion of people living in households with income below a defined threshold or claiming benefits relating to low incomes. The indicators used for the income domain were:
  • Adults & children in income support households
  • Adults & children in pension credit households
  • Adults & children in income-based job seekers allowance households
  • Adults & children in tax credit (child tax credit and working tax credit) households below a low income threshold
  • National Asylum Support Service (NASS) supported asylum seekers in Wales in receipt of subsistence only and accommodation support

UKBB:Pulse wave peak to peak time.name: Pulse wave peak to peak time
UKBB:Pulse wave peak to peak time.text:
peak to peak time in milliseconds

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. peak to peak time is the difference between the peak values of direct and reflected components.

UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wale.name: Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wales)
UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wale.text:
The Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation 2008 is the official measure of deprivation for small areas in Wales. It was developed for the Welsh Assembly Government by the Assembly's Statistical Directorate and the Local Government Data Unit (Wales).

The WIMD 2008 is made up of eight separate domains (or kinds) of deprivation: income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, and community safety.

Each of them was based on a range of different indicators which meant that they were measured in different ways using different units. So before they could be combined the measurements had to be transformed to make them compatible. For example, if the height of something had been measured in metres and the weight in kilograms it would not make sense simply to add them together.

Income and employment were classed as the most important factors, and they were given the biggest weighting in the overall index. Although there is more to deprivation than poverty, not having enough money or a job is a big part of it.

If the participant was uncertain of the type of cancer they had had, then they described it to the interviewer (a trained nurse) who attempted to place it within the coding tree. If the cancer could not be located in the coding tree then the interviewer entered a free-text description of it. These free-text descriptions were subsequently examined by a doctor and, where possible, matched to entries in the coding tree. Free-text descriptions which could not be matched with very high probability have been marked as "unclassifiable".

UKBB:Pulse wave pressure versus time res.name: Pulse wave pressure versus time response curve
UKBB:Pulse wave pressure versus time res.text:
Wave data containing 3 waveforms, each consisting of one direct and one reflected component.

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. Each waveform is actually a single pulse with 100 points. Since the heart rate is in beats per minute, a single beat takes 60seconds / Heart Rate and time between two beats is (60/Heart Rate)/100.

The data is formatted as follows:

  • The first number (i.e. digits before the first '|' character)indicate the number of points X,Y for the curve.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated by a '|' character from the preceding/succeeding pair.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated internally by a ',' character.
The X-axis is the time in milliseconds and the Y-axis is the Pulse signal strength in arbitrary units.

conceptGroups.concept: Self-reported race and/or ethnicity or ancestry/ethnic origin (select all that apply, with free-text option)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Race and/or Ethnicity: Captures the self-reported racial and/or ethnic identity of the participant, answering 'How would you describe your race and/or ethnicity or ancestry/ethnic origin?' Answer type is a combination of structured categorical selection (select all that apply) from a standardized value set — including American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian, Black or African American, Middle Eastern, North African, Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, White or Caucasian, and Other — plus an optional free-text field for specific ancestry or ethnic origin detail (e.g., Italian, Haitian, Cherokee, Korean). Source is self-report. The concept spans both broad racial categories and specific ethnic/ancestral origins, and the ideal CDE accommodates multi-select (check all that apply) as the primary response mode, with a single best-fit option as an alternative summary, and a free-text write-in for granular ancestry.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported race, ethnicity, or ancestry of the participant

conceptGroups.concept: Diastolic blood pressure measurement (numeric, mmHg)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Diastolic blood pressure measurement: 'What is the diastolic blood pressure?' Numeric value in millimeters of mercury (mmHg), integer or decimal. No single qualifier is uniformly specified across member fields; fields carry reading-instance qualifiers (first reading [bp1], second reading [bp2]), indicating this CDE may need to be instantiated per measurement occasion. No laterality, posture, or subject qualifier is consistently specified in the source fields.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Seated or resting diastolic blood pressure measurement in mmHg, captured as a single reading or one of multiple sequential readings.

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of specific cancer type: which biological relatives have been diagnosed (per cancer type)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Family history of cancer by cancer type and biological relative: For each specific cancer type (e.g., bladder cancer, blood/soft tissue cancer, bone cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer, and other cancer types), identifies which biological family members have been diagnosed with that cancer. The question asked is 'Who in your family has had [cancer type]? Select all that apply.' Answer type is a multi-select checkbox allowing simultaneous selection of one or more biological relatives from a fixed set of options: Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent (and potentially other relatives). Each cancer type is captured as a separate item, and each response is a set of zero or more relative-type values. No laterality, body-site sub-qualifier, or time-window qualifier is specified; the subject is the participant's biological family members (not the participant themselves).
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Family history of a specific type of cancer (select all that apply), where the cancer type varies across items

conceptGroups.concept: Neighborhood walkability perception: multi-item self-report scale (aesthetics, sidewalk presence, sidewalk maintenance, daytime crime safety, nighttime crime safety, traffic, physical activity visibility) rated on 4-point Likert agreement scale
conceptGroups.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability perception: a multi-item self-report instrument assessing the respondent's perceived walkability of their own neighborhood across key domains including aesthetic appeal (interesting things to look at), sidewalk presence, sidewalk maintenance/condition, and daytime and nighttime walking safety related to crime. Each item is answered on a 4-point Likert agreement scale (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree) with additional response options for 'Does not apply to my neighborhood,' 'Don't know/Not sure,' and 'Prefer not to say.' The unit of measurement is ordinal agreement rating per item; items may be summed or averaged into a composite walkability perception score. Qualifier: self-report about respondent's own residential neighborhood.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Perceived neighborhood walkability barriers due to crime rate or traffic making walking unsafe or unpleasant

conceptGroups.concept: Body Mass Index numeric value (kg/m²)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body composition and weight status assessment: a cluster of measures capturing (1) calculated Body Mass Index (BMI, kg/m²), (2) measured body weight in kilograms (numeric/text entry), (3) DXA-derived assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water from AGC scan (decimal, %), (4) DXA-derived assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water from WBC scan (decimal, %), and (5) self-perceived weight status (categorical: Overweight | Underweight | Just about right). Together these fields answer: 'What is the participant's body size, body composition, and self-assessed weight status?' Answer types range across calculated numeric (BMI, kg/m²), continuous numeric (weight, kg), decimal percentage (DXA LBM water fraction, %), and ordinal categorical (self-perception: 1=Overweight, 2=Underweight, 3=Just about right). Note: DXA water-in-LBM fields carry distinct scanner/protocol qualifiers (AGC vs. WBC), and the self-perception field is self-reported by the participant.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Body Mass Index (BMI) measurement across cohort visits and sub-studies

conceptGroups.concept: Respondent's highest educational attainment (level/degree completed)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported): the highest grade, level of schooling, or academic/vocational degree or diploma the respondent has completed or received. Answers the question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have obtained?' Expected answer type: ordinal categorical, encoded as a single ordered scale spanning no formal schooling through advanced post-secondary degrees, with categories covering: (1) never attended / kindergarten only; (2) elementary grades 1–8; (3) secondary/high school grades 9–12 without diploma; (4) high school diploma or equivalent (e.g., GED); (5) some post-secondary without credential; (6) trade/vocational certificate or diploma; (7) non-university college diploma (e.g., community college, CEGEP); (8) bachelor's degree; (9) graduate or professional degree (master's, doctorate, professional). No laterality, body-site, or condition qualifier is present; the subject is the respondent (self). Units: none (categorical ordinal).
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Highest level of education or degree completed by the participant

conceptGroups.concept: Average number of cigarettes smoked per day (current or historical)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Average daily cigarette consumption: captures the typical number of cigarettes smoked per day, either currently or over the lifetime smoking period (fields span both current and historical/average-over-entire-smoking-period contexts). The question asks: 'On average, how many cigarettes do/did you smoke per day?' Answer type: numeric integer (count of cigarettes per day), with 20 cigarettes equaling 1 pack as a reference unit; may be collected as a free-text number entry or ordinal range (e.g., 1–10, 11–20, 21–30, 31–40, 41–50, >50); permissible non-numeric responses include 'Don't know' and 'Prefer not to answer'. Note: member fields carry two distinct time-window qualifiers — current daily cigarette count and average daily cigarette count over the entire past smoking history — which should be treated as separate CDEs if time window precision is required.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Average number of cigarettes smoked per day (current or over lifetime smoking history)

conceptGroups.concept: Visual acuity letter score and LogMAR under mesopic and photopic conditions for each eye (OD and OS)

conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Visual acuity measurements (letter scores and LogMAR scores) recorded under mesopic and photopic conditions for both eyes (OD and OS)

Each item is answered by the subject about themselves. Question form: 'Has a doctor ever told you that you have [condition]?' Answer type: categorical binary (Yes / No), with optional 'Prefer not to say' / refusal option per item.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported history of cardiac conditions (heart attack/MI, heart disease/CHF, or angina) as distinct diagnosis categories
coherenceDistinctValues: heart disease including congestive heart failure
angina / chest pain due to heart disease

conceptGroups.concept: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication) structured symptom assessment (Rose/Edinburgh Questionnaire items)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication) symptom assessment: a structured set of binary and categorical items characterizing walking-induced leg or buttock pain, including (1) presence of pain in leg or buttock while walking (Yes/No), (2) anatomical location of pain — whether it includes the calf/calves (Pain includes calf/calves | Pain does not include calf/calves), (3) whether leg pain ever disappears while continuing to walk (Yes/No), (4) predominant side of leg pain (Right | Left | Both), and (5) whether leg pain occurs when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground (Yes/No). Collectively these items screen for intermittent claudication consistent with peripheral arterial disease. Answer types are binary (0=No/1=Yes) or nominal categorical as specified; no continuous units required.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Characterization of leg/buttock pain symptoms during walking or rest, including location, laterality, onset, and behavior of pain consistent with claudication assessment

conceptGroups.concept: Body weight numeric value
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body composition and weight status assessment: a cluster of measures capturing (1) calculated Body Mass Index (BMI, kg/m²), (2) measured body weight in kilograms (numeric/text entry), (3) DXA-derived assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water from AGC scan (decimal, %), (4) DXA-derived assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water from WBC scan (decimal, %), and (5) self-perceived weight status (categorical: Overweight | Underweight | Just about right). Together these fields answer: 'What is the participant's body size, body composition, and self-assessed weight status?' Answer types range across calculated numeric (BMI, kg/m²), continuous numeric (weight, kg), decimal percentage (DXA LBM water fraction, %), and ordinal categorical (self-perception: 1=Overweight, 2=Underweight, 3=Just about right). Note: DXA water-in-LBM fields carry distinct scanner/protocol qualifiers (AGC vs. WBC), and the self-perception field is self-reported by the participant.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Participant body weight measured or reported in pounds or kilograms

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of specific circulatory conditions — which biological relatives affected (per condition: CHF, CAD, heart attack, heart valve disease, hypertension, and omnibus cardiovascular conditions)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Circulatory condition history — a cluster of CDEs capturing both personal and family history of specific circulatory conditions (congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease, heart attack). For personal history: age at first diagnosis reported in life-stage categories (Child 0–11, Adolescent 12–17, Adult 18–64, Older Adult 65+); answer type is ordinal categorical radio selection, one per condition. For family history: which biological relatives (Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, and potentially others) have had each named condition; answer type is multi-select checkbox (select all that apply), one set per condition. The personal-history fields are self-reported (subject = self); the family-history fields are reported by the participant about their biological family members. Conditions covered include at minimum: congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease (including angina), and heart attack.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Family history of specific circulatory/heart conditions (select all that apply), capturing which relatives have had a given cardiac or vascular diagnosis
coherenceDistinctValues: any heart and blood condition (umbrella screen)

conceptGroups.concept: Self-reported standing height without shoes (ordinal foot-and-inch bands, cm equivalents)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Self-reported standing height without shoes: captures the respondent's own height measured without footwear, answering 'How tall are you without shoes on?' Answer type: continuous numeric value in centimeters (cm), collected via self-report; source fields use coded ordinal ranges spanning approximately 1'0" to 6'11"+ (roughly 29–215 cm) encoded as foot-and-inch bands with corresponding cm equivalents, but the ideal CDE records height as a single numeric value in centimeters (or decimal inches) to enable precise analysis. Subject qualifier: self (the respondent). No laterality or body-site qualifier applies.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Trimmed height measurements (repeated/numbered trials) from the CLSA HWT module, each part of a skip pattern

conceptGroups.concept: Online mental health/well-being questionnaire administration date (invitation sent, module start, module completion)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Online mental health/well-being questionnaire administration date: captures the calendar date associated with a participant's engagement with an online mental health or well-being questionnaire, encompassing invitation sent date, module start date, and module completion date. Question answered: 'What is the date on which the online mental health/well-being questionnaire (or a specified module thereof) was initiated, completed, or for which an invitation was dispatched?' Answer type: ISO 8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD), with a required qualifier specifying the event type (invitation sent / questionnaire started / questionnaire completed) and, where applicable, the module name (e.g., General Health, Mental Health).
memberVariableNames: UKBB:Date of completing mental health questionnaire

conceptGroups.concept: Digital Volume Pulse (DVP) waveform morphology decomposition measurements (notch position, peak position, shoulder position, peak-to-peak time, raw waveform data, reflection index)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Digital Volume Pulse (DVP) waveform morphology measurement: captures the decomposed components of a finger photoplethysmographic (DVP) waveform, which is modeled as the sum of a direct (forward) pressure wave from the left ventricle and a reflected wave returning from the lower body via the aorta. The CDE encompasses the following sub-elements derived from the DVP waveform decomposition: (1) position of the notch on the waveform (sample index or normalized time at which the notch between direct and reflected components occurs); (2) position of the peak on the waveform (sample index or normalized time of the overall waveform peak); (3) position of the shoulder on the waveform (sample index or normalized time of the inflection/shoulder marking the onset of the reflected component); (4) peak-to-peak time between the direct and reflected component peaks (milliseconds); and (5) raw wave data comprising 3 representative DVP waveform cycles, each containing one direct and one reflected component (time-series amplitude array, arbitrary photoplethysmographic units, sampled at device-specific rate). Question answered: 'What are the morphological and temporal characteristics of the decomposed digital volume pulse waveform recorded at the finger?' Answer type: mixed — integer or floating-point sample indices or normalized positional values for waveform landmark positions; numeric continuous value in milliseconds for peak-to-peak time; time-series array of numeric amplitude values for raw waveform data.
memberVariableNames: UKBB:Position of the pulse wave peak
UKBB:Position of the shoulder on the pulse waveform
UKBB:Pulse wave peak to peak time
UKBB:Pulse wave pressure versus time response curve
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Measurements derived from the digital volume pulse waveform characterizing the direct and reflected pressure wave components (peak position, notch position, shoulder position, peak-to-peak time, waveform curve, and reflection index).

conceptGroups.concept: Current marital/partner status (self-report, categorical)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Current marital/partner status: a single-item self-report measure capturing the participant's present legal and cohabitation relationship status. Question: 'What is your current marital/partner status?' Answer type: categorical (enumerated), with response options minimally covering: Married; Living with a partner/common-law relationship; Single/Never married and never lived with a partner; Separated; Divorced; Widowed; Prefer not to answer. No laterality, body-site, or subject qualifier beyond self-report (participant's own status).
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Current or baseline marital/partner status of the participant

conceptGroups.concept: Assistive device use in past 12 months (binary), stratified by body region (hand/upper extremity, leg/lower extremity, neck/back) and device source (commercial vs. custom/prescribed)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Assistive device use in the past 12 months, stratified by body region (hand/upper extremity, leg/lower extremity, neck/back) and device type (commercial vs. custom/prescribed): 'During the past 12 months, have you used any assistive devices?' — answered separately for each combination of body region and device source category. Binary response per item (1=Yes, 0=No).
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Use of assistive devices (hand/arm brace, leg brace/supportive device, or other assistive device based on open-text responses) as recorded in the CLSA dataset

conceptGroups.concept: Currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for a specified medical condition (Yes/No)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Current prescribed medication and/or treatment status for a specified medical condition. Asks: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for [condition]?' where [condition] is a condition-specific qualifier (e.g., stroke, acid reflux, celiac disease, colon polyps, chronic lung disease — each instantiated as a separate CDE item). Answer type: binary categorical (Yes / No). Each CDE instance carries the specific condition name as a required qualifier; the set of member fields represents condition-specific instantiations of this single reusable template rather than a single merged element.

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of diabetes (by relative and diabetes type)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Family and personal history of diabetes (any type): a set of CDEs capturing (1) whether the respondent's first-degree relatives (mother, father, sibling, son, daughter) have been diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes, Type 2 diabetes, or other/unknown diabetes — answered per relative via multi-select checkbox or per-relative yes/no radio (values: Yes | No | Unknown | Prefer not to say); (2) whether either parent specifically has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes (radio: Yes | No | Unknown | Prefer not to say); (3) whether a sibling specifically has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes (radio: Yes | No | Unknown | Prefer not to say); and (4) the respondent's own age at first diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes, captured as an ordinal life-stage category (Child [0–11] | Adolescent [12–17] | Adult [18–64] | Older Adult [65–74] | 75+). The concept spans self-reported personal diagnosis age and first-degree family history across three diabetes subtypes (Type 1, Type 2, other/unknown), with the subject qualifier varying across fields: self (age at diagnosis), parents as a pair, individual first-degree relatives (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son).

conceptGroups.concept: Sex at birth — other free-text specification
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sex at birth — other (free-text specification): Captures the participant's self-reported sex assigned at birth when it does not correspond to standard response options (e.g., male, female, intersex). Answers the question: 'If you selected 'None of these' or 'Other' for sex assigned at birth, please specify.' Expected answer type: free-text string.

conceptGroups.concept: Free-text specification of other mental health or substance use condition(s) for a specific family member (daughter, father, mother, sibling, son)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Family history of mental health or substance use conditions (blood relatives): a multi-part CDE set capturing (1) which mental health or substance use conditions (e.g., alcohol use disorder, anxiety/panic disorder, depression, autism spectrum disorder, and others) have been diagnosed in the participant's blood relatives — answered as a multi-select checklist of condition categories; (2) for each endorsed condition, which specific biological family members are affected (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, etc.) — answered as a multi-select checklist of relationship types per condition; and (3) the participant's own age at first diagnosis of any other (unspecified) mental health or substance use condition — answered as an ordinal radio selection (Child 0–11, Adolescent 12–17, Adult 18–64, or older adult category). Answer types: checkbox (multi-select) for condition presence and affected relatives; ordinal categorical for self-reported age-at-diagnosis of residual conditions. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified; context is self-reported family history by blood relation.

conceptGroups.concept: Number of servings of a specific food item consumed (dietary recall/food frequency), categorical ordinal
conceptGroups.idealCde: Number of servings of a specific food item consumed during a dietary recall or food frequency assessment, asked conditionally upon reported consumption of that food category. The CDE captures serving quantity for an individual food or food group (e.g., baked beans, coleslaw/salad vegetables in mayonnaise, crumble topping, fried/roast potatoes, or other beans/pulses/lentils). Question: 'How many servings of [specific food item] did you have?' Answer type: Categorical single-select ordinal representing serving count in standardized units (Serving), with values spanning fractional portions (quarter, half) through whole servings (1, 2) up to a maximum/ceiling category (3+ or 4+), encoded as discrete ordered categories (e.g., quarter=0.25, half=0.5, 1=1, 2=2, 3+=3 or more, 4+=4 or more).

conceptGroups.concept: Electronic nicotine product / e-cigarette / vape use — ever and current use status
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and nicotine product use status — self-reported current and lifetime use of non-cigarette nicotine delivery products (traditional cigars/cigarillos/filtered cigars and electronic nicotine products/e-cigarettes/vapes) by the participant themselves; captures (1) ever-use (lifetime history: Yes / No / Don't know / Prefer not to answer), (2) current use status (Every day / Some days / Not at all / Don't know / Prefer not to answer), assessed separately for each product category (combustible cigars and electronic nicotine products); answer type: categorical/ordinal radio-button response per product type, with standard 'Prefer not to answer' and 'Don't know' escape options; no units; subject qualifier: self (participant); no laterality or body-site qualifier; time qualifiers: lifetime (ever) and current (now).

conceptGroups.concept: Specific types of sedentary sitting activities performed (multi-select: e.g. bingewatching, computer use, crafts/hobbies, handheld device use, listening)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sedentary sitting activities (specific types): Among time spent sitting, what specific activities were performed? Select all that apply. Answer type: multiple-response categorical (select all that apply); response options include activity categories such as: bingewatching/screen viewing, computer use, crafts/hobbies, handheld device use, listening (to music/radio/podcasts), and other sedentary sitting activities. Each selected activity is coded as a separate binary indicator or multi-select response. Context: self-reported sedentary behavior activity type inventory, no specific time window stated in source fields.

conceptGroups.concept: Sex of participant (general/self-reported, not explicitly at birth)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sex assigned at birth: captures the biological sex recorded on the participant's original birth certificate or assigned at birth. Answers the question 'What sex were you assigned at birth?' Expected answer type: categorical (enumerated); response options must include at minimum: Male, Female, Intersex, with recommended additional options for 'None of these describe me / Other' and 'Prefer not to answer'. Note: one member field ('What is the sex of person #2?') carries a different qualifier — it refers to a household member (person #2), not the primary respondent — and should be treated as a distinct CDE rather than harmonized with self-reported sex assigned at birth.

conceptGroups.concept: Percentage of population aged 25+ with at minimum a high school diploma or equivalent (geographic/population-level aggregate measure)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Educational attainment at the population level among adults aged 25 and older: captures the percentage of the population aged 25+ who have attained at minimum a high school diploma or equivalent. Question answered: 'What percentage of adults aged 25 and older in the defined geographic area have completed at least a high school-level education?' Answer type: Numeric, expressed as a percentage (0–100%).

conceptGroups.concept: Chronic pain by body site — self-reported presence of pain at a specified anatomical location lasting more than 3 months (Yes/No/Do not know/Prefer not to answer)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Chronic pain by body site (duration >3 months) — self-reported presence of persistent pain at a specified anatomical location (back / hip / neck or shoulder / stomach or abdominal / all over the body) lasting more than 3 months, asked among participants who reported activity-interfering pain at that site in the past month; question: 'Have you had [site-specific] pains for more than 3 months?'; answer type: categorical single — Yes | No | Do not know | Prefer not to answer; note: member fields carry different body-site qualifiers (back, hip, neck/shoulder, stomach/abdominal, whole body) and each constitutes a distinct site-specific instance of this CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Numeric food group intake scores for vegetables (cruciferous, dark yellow, green leafy, other)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary fat and sugar intake frequency: A self-reported dietary behavior assessment capturing how often an individual consumes high-fat and high-sugar foods and beverages, including regular (non-low-fat) snack chips/crackers, desserts/sweets, added fats (butter, margarine, or meat fat used as seasoning or spread), and fruit juice. The CDE answers: 'How frequently do you consume specific high-fat or high-sugar food items?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale per item, with response options ranging across consumption frequency categories (e.g., rarely/never, less than once per week, 1 time or less per week, 2–3 times per week, 4 or more times per week, per day/week/month/year as applicable), plus a 'Prefer not to say' option; administered as a multi-item self-report questionnaire with one ordinal response per food/beverage category. No laterality, body site, or specific subject qualifier is specified beyond self-report.

conceptGroups.concept: Heart rate (pulse rate) in beats per minute at clinical encounter
conceptGroups.idealCde: Heart rate (pulse rate): the number of heartbeats per minute measured at a clinical encounter. Question: 'What is the patient's heart rate?' Answer type: numeric integer; units: beats per minute (bpm).

conceptGroups.concept: Number of drinks per week (current and/or former drinkers)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Alcohol Use History and Consumption Pattern — A composite domain capturing self-reported lifetime and recent alcohol use behavior for the participant (self-report). Covers: (1) Lifetime alcohol use ever (yes/no/prefer not to answer); (2) Total years of alcohol consumption (numeric years, with upper-bound category >60 years); (3) Frequency of heavy episodic drinking (6+ drinks on one occasion) in the past year (ordinal: never in last year / less than monthly / monthly / weekly / daily or almost daily); (4) Typical number of drinks consumed per drinking day (ordinal: 1–2 / 3–4 / 5–6 / 7–9 / 10 or more). All items include a 'Prefer not to answer' option. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier; subject is the participant themselves. Answer types: binary radio (lifetime use), numeric/dropdown (years), ordinal frequency radio (heavy episodic), ordinal quantity radio (typical daily drinks).

conceptGroups.concept: Lifetime cigarette smoking status: whether smoked ≥100 cigarettes in lifetime
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and nicotine product use history — a set of CDEs capturing lifetime use of combustible cigarettes and electronic nicotine delivery systems (e-cigarettes/vaping devices). Covers: (1) Lifetime cigarette smoking status: whether the individual has smoked ≥100 cigarettes (≥5 packs) in their lifetime [radio; Yes / No / Prefer not to say]; (2) Age at smoking initiation: age in whole years when the individual first started smoking cigarettes [integer, years; with upper-bound category '>60 years' and 'Prefer not to say']; (3) Total years of cigarette smoking: cumulative number of years the individual has smoked cigarettes [integer, years; with upper-bound category '>60 years' and 'Prefer not to say']; (4) Age at vaping/e-cigarette initiation: age in whole years when the individual first started vaping or using e-cigarettes [integer, years; with upper-bound category '>60 years' and 'Prefer not to say']; (5) Total years of vaping/e-cigarette use: cumulative number of years the individual has vaped or used e-cigarettes [integer, years; with upper-bound category '>20 years' and 'Prefer not to say']. All items are self-reported and pertain to the respondent's own lifetime history with no specific time-window restriction.
memberVariableNames: UKBB:Light smokers, at least 100 smokes in lifetime

conceptGroups.concept: Habitual fruit consumption frequency/quantity
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary intake frequency/quantity assessment capturing habitual consumption of fruits, vegetables, and fast food. The CDE answers: 'How often or how many servings of fruits and/or vegetables do you typically consume per day or per week, and how often do you consume fast food meals or snacks per week?' The member fields span three distinct sub-concepts: (1) fast food frequency per week (ordinal: <1 time, 1–3 times, 4+ times), (2) daily fruit servings (ordinal or numeric count), (3) daily vegetable servings (ordinal or numeric count), and (4) combined daily fruit-and-vegetable servings (ordinal or numeric count). Because the source fields carry different qualifiers — fast food weekly frequency vs. fruit-only daily servings vs. vegetable-only daily servings vs. combined fruit-and-vegetable daily servings — the ideal CDE set should preserve these as separate elements rather than collapsing them. Each element should offer either an ordinal response scale (e.g., rarely/none, 1–3 servings, 4–5 servings, 5+ servings for produce; <1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4+ times/week for fast food) or a free-text numeric entry (servings per day or times per week), with a 'Prefer not to say' option. Reference period is 'typical day' or 'typical week.' Answer type: ordinal categorical or non-negative integer count; units: servings per day (produce) or eating occasions per week (fast food).

conceptGroups.concept: Frequency of ADHD-related symptom interference with work or education functioning
conceptGroups.idealCde: This source concept groups heterogeneous psychosocial and socioeconomic self-report items that do not share a single underlying construct; the member fields span at least five distinct measurement domains: (1) Perceived job mobility — the respondent's self-assessed ease of finding equivalent employment elsewhere, answered on a 3-point ordinal scale (Very easy / Somewhat easy / Not easy at all) plus Don't know / Prefer not to say / Not applicable; (2) Pre-retirement income adequacy expectation — the respondent's retrospective appraisal of whether household income and investments were expected to maintain their standard of living before retirement, answered on a 3-point ordinal scale (Adequate / Barely adequate / Inadequate); (3) Work- or school-based social network size — the count of people the respondent knows personally by name through work or school (excluding family, close friends, and neighbours), answered as a non-negative integer (count of persons); (4) Frequency of participation in educational and cultural activities involving others (e.g., courses, concerts, plays, museum visits) in the past 12 months, answered on a 6-point ordinal frequency scale (At least once a day / At least once a week / At least once a month / At least once a year / Never); (5) Lifetime and recent history of marital separation or divorce since age 16, answered as a 3-level categorical (No never / Yes but not in the last 12 months / Yes within the last 12 months) plus Prefer not to answer. Because these fields measure fundamentally different constructs, the ideal representation is five separate CDEs rather than one; if a single CDE must be chosen, it should be defined as a structured psychosocial profile instrument capturing employment mobility perception, retirement financial adequacy expectation, work/school social network size, cultural activity participation frequency, and marital disruption history, each as a distinct response element with its own answer type (ordinal categorical, ordinal categorical, integer count, ordinal frequency, and categorical lifetime/recent event respectively), all self-reported by the study participant with no laterality, body-site, or condition qualifier specified.

conceptGroups.concept: Diabetes or pre-diabetes diagnosis status (ever told by doctor / current diagnosis, Yes/No/Unknown)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Diabetes or Pre-diabetes Status: A yes/no indicator of whether an individual has been diagnosed with Type II diabetes or pre-diabetes (borderline diabetes / elevated blood sugar), as confirmed by a clinician or self-reported. The CDE answers the question: 'Has this person ever been told by a doctor that they have diabetes, borderline diabetes, or pre-diabetes, or do they have a current diagnosis of Type II diabetes or pre-diabetes?' Expected answer type: categorical/boolean (Yes / No / Unknown), with optional sub-classification distinguishing Type II Diabetes from Pre-diabetes as a coded enumeration. Note: one member field additionally captures emotional burden (distress about living with diabetes) on a 5-point Likert scale, and one member field captures incident onset since a prior study visit — these represent distinct sub-concepts (psychosocial impact and incident status, respectively) that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than collapsed into a single diagnosis-status element.

conceptGroups.concept: Reason contributed to decision to retire (categorical yes/no per reason)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Retirement reason — health/disability contribution: A categorical or binary CDE capturing whether health, stress, or disability (physical and/or emotional/mental) was a contributing reason to the respondent's decision to retire (or return to work after retirement). The primary question is: 'Did health, stress, or disability contribute to your decision to retire (or return to work after retirement)?' with a follow-up distinguishing the type: physical health, emotional/mental health (including stress), or both. Answer type: binary Yes/No for contribution (1=Yes, 0=No), with a conditional categorical sub-item (1=Physical health; 2=Emotional/mental health including stress; 3=Both physical and emotional/mental health). Qualifier: self-reported; pertains to the respondent's own retirement decision and, where applicable, their decision to return to work after initial retirement.

conceptGroups.concept: Area-level income/multiple deprivation score or proportion for a small geographic area (LSOA or equivalent)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Area-level income deprivation score or proportion: captures the extent of income deprivation within a small area (LSOA or equivalent), answering 'What proportion of the population in this geographic area is experiencing income deprivation (i.e., living in low-income households or claiming income-related benefits)?'. Answer type: numeric proportion or score (continuous, typically expressed as a rate between 0 and 1, or as a ranked/decile index value), attributed to a defined small-area geographic unit (e.g., LSOA in England or Wales). Derived from aggregated counts of individuals in income-deprived households across multiple benefit/low-income indicators; no individual-level qualifier — unit of analysis is the area, not a specific person.

conceptGroups.concept: Self-reported overall/general health status (5-point Excellent–Poor scale)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Self-reported general health status: captures both overall physical health and mental health as distinct self-assessments. For overall/physical health: 'In general, would you say your health is excellent, very good, good, fair, or poor?' For mental health specifically: 'In general, how would you rate your mental health, including your mood and your ability to think?' Both items use a 5-point ordinal Likert scale with response options: Excellent, Very Good, Good, Fair, Poor (self-reported by the participant). Note: the source fields include a general/physical health variant and a mental health-specific variant — these should be captured as two separate CDEs or clearly distinguished sub-elements rather than collapsed into one, as they measure distinct constructs (overall/physical perceived health vs. perceived mental health).

conceptGroups.concept: Snellen fraction visual acuity by laterality (OD/OS) and luminance condition (mesopic/photopic)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Visual acuity expressed as a Snellen fraction, measured under both mesopic (low-light) and photopic (normal-light) luminance conditions, for each eye separately (right eye [OD] and left eye [OS]). The CDE answers: 'What is the Snellen fraction visual acuity for the specified eye under the specified lighting condition?' Answer type: text string representing a Snellen fraction (e.g., '20/20', '20/40'); qualifiers required: laterality (OD / OS) and luminance condition (mesopic / photopic).

conceptGroups.concept: Participant's current marital or relationship status (self-reported)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Marital Status: The participant's current legal and/or cohabitation relationship status. Question: 'What is your current marital or relationship status?' Answer type: Categorical (single-select); recommended values: Married | Living with partner/domestic partner | Widowed | Divorced | Separated | Never married/Single | Other | Prefer not to answer. No qualifier specified (self-reported by participant).

conceptGroups.concept: Participant body height measurement in centimeters
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body height measurement: 'What is the participant's height?' Numeric value in centimeters (cm). Continuous numeric type, units = cm. Cluster also includes a paired protocol-modification flag ('Was a protocol modification made for the height measurement?') captured as a binary indicator (0=No, 1=Yes).

conceptGroups.concept: Languages in which respondent can conduct a conversation (per-language Yes/No flags across multiple languages)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Language background and English proficiency: A multi-component CDE capturing (1) the respondent's primary/first language (free-text or coded language name), (2) whether English is the respondent's first language (Yes/No/Prefer not to say), (3) whether a language other than English is spoken at home (Yes/No/Prefer not to say), (4) the respondent's self-rated English-speaking proficiency when a non-English home language is reported (ordinal: Very well / Well / Not well / Not at all / Don't know / Prefer not to say), and (5) the specific languages in which the respondent can conduct a conversation (multi-select or binary flags per language, including Arabic as an explicitly enumerated option). Answers are self-reported by the participant; no laterality, body-site, or condition qualifier is specified. The concept addresses the respondent's own linguistic background, home language environment, and functional English fluency.

conceptGroups.concept: Age (banded) when respondent was first told they had Type 2 diabetes
conceptGroups.idealCde: Family and personal history of diabetes (any type): a set of CDEs capturing (1) whether the respondent's first-degree relatives (mother, father, sibling, son, daughter) have been diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes, Type 2 diabetes, or other/unknown diabetes — answered per relative via multi-select checkbox or per-relative yes/no radio (values: Yes | No | Unknown | Prefer not to say); (2) whether either parent specifically has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes (radio: Yes | No | Unknown | Prefer not to say); (3) whether a sibling specifically has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes (radio: Yes | No | Unknown | Prefer not to say); and (4) the respondent's own age at first diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes, captured as an ordinal life-stage category (Child [0–11] | Adolescent [12–17] | Adult [18–64] | Older Adult [65–74] | 75+). diff.embedText: The English Indices of Deprivation 2010 are measures of multiple deprivation at the small area level. The model of multiple deprivation which underpins the Indices of Deprivation 2010 is based on the idea of distinct domains of deprivation which can be recognised and measured separately. These domains are experienced by individuals living in an area. People may be counted in one or more of the domains, depending on the number of types of deprivation that they experience. Each domain represents a specific form of deprivation experienced by people and each can be measured individually using a number of indicators. Seven distinct domains have been identified in the English Indices of Deprivation; Income Deprivation, Employment Deprivation, Health Deprivation and Disability, Education Skills and Training Deprivation, Barriers to Housing and Services, Living Environment Deprivation, and Crime. Individual domains can be used in isolation as measures of each specific form of deprivation. They can also be combined, using appropriate weights, into a single overall Index of Multiple Deprivation which can be used to rank every small area in England according to the deprivation experienced by the people living there. Along with two supplementary indices, Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index and Income Deprivation Affecting Older People Index, they form the English Indices of Deprivation. These statistics allow the most, and least, deprived areas of the country to be identified as well as providing information about the issues faced by people living in different parts of the country.

diff.embedText: peak to peak time in milliseconds A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route.
